title: Generic closed-fibre image of a flat chart over the changed base
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\varphi:A\to B$ a local homomorphism, $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a smooth scheme morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and $X=L\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $n\geq0$ let $P=B[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and $C:B\to P$ be the constant-series map. Suppose $t:\operatorname{Spec}P\to X$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and $\operatorname{pr}_B\circ t=\operatorname{Spec}C$. There are a point $v\in\operatorname{Spec}P$ with prime ideal $\mathfrak m_B P$, an affine open $V$ in the closed fibre $L_{\mathfrak m_A}$, and $x\in V$, such that $(\operatorname{pr}_L\circ t)(v)$ equals the image of $x$ in $L$, and the closure of $\{x\}$ in $V$ is an irreducible component of $V$. Spectra and scheme topology are those of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal of B is the maximal ideal of A; no flatness of $\varphi$ or section is assumed.

proof.text: Use finite generation of m_B to identify P/m_B P with kappa(B)[[X]]: lift coefficients for surjectivity and write coefficients in a fixed finite set of generators for the kernel equality. The quotient is a domain, including n=0, so m_B P defines v. Its contraction to B is m_B, and localness contracts that to m_A.

Restrict t by base change to the closed fibre over B. This is flat because t is flat over X. Identify the target with the original closed fibre of q base changed to kappa(B). Projection to the original closed fibre is flat since kappa(B) over kappa(A) is a field extension. Compose to obtain a flat map from the spectrum of the power-series domain over kappa(B) to the original fibre. Its zero-ideal point maps to the fibre point eta whose image in L is pr_L(t(v)).

Choose an affine neighbourhood V of eta. Going down for the flat map shows that eta has no strict generalization: a generalization would lift to one of the zero-ideal point of the domain, which has none. In V this says its prime ideal is minimal. The closure of the corresponding point x is therefore an irreducible component of V. The fibre topology and residue-field base change used here are scheme-theoretic, not merely a topological factorization.

theorem exists_flat_power_series_chart_generic_image
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {L : Scheme.{u}} (q : L ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [Smooth q]
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom φ]
    (n : ℕ) (t : Spec (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) B)) ⟶
      Limits.pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) [Flat t]
    (ht : t ≫ Limits.pullback.snd q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)) =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPowerSeries.C (σ := Fin n)))) :
    ∃ (v : Spec (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) B)))
      (V : (q.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)).Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (x : V),
      v.asIdeal = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B).map (MvPowerSeries.C (σ := Fin n)) ∧
      (t ≫ Limits.pullback.fst q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) v =
        q.fiberι (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) (V.ι x) ∧
      closure ({x} : Set V) ∈ irreducibleComponents V
